title: Low-degree mass and stable influence
statement: Let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, let $i$ be a coordinate, and let $k$ be a natural number. For any real $[0m\rho$ with $0<\rho\leq 1$, the low-degree coordinate mass of $f$ at $i$ through degree $k$ is at most $\rho^{-k}$ times the stable influence of the real-valued version of $f$ at $i$ with parameter $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube
